params._comment: Rerun of l3_interaction_grid (2026-09-18 check-in). The first run silently corrupted half its data: plan_interaction_levels.py cast neighbour_confirmation_count's worst value to float (1.0), and settling-eval's Go config unmarshal rejects a non-integer for that field, so all 48 rows at neighbour_confirmation_count=1.0 errored (24/24 sites x 2 noise_relative levels) while the process still exited 0 and the supervisor recorded the stage 'done'. Fixed at the root (plan_interaction_levels.py's new IS_INT cast, plus a defensive int-cast in run_interaction_grid.py's make_multi_config) and in the supervisor (handle_l3_interaction_grid now fails the stage if any combo has zero non-error rows, instead of trusting exit code alone). This rerun reuses the same handler/scripts; run_interaction_grid.py's dedup is keyed on the combo id string, and 'neighbour_confirmation_count=1' (int) differs from the old broken 'neighbour_confirmation_count=1.0' (float), so it will only execute the previously-broken combos and leave the 48 already-good rows untouched.

Deterministic additive-vs-compounding verdict (analyze_interaction_grid.py) over the corrected interaction-results.csv: does pushing neighbour_confirmation_count and noise_relative to their worst values together compound, cancel, or stay additive relative to their single-key effects from Batch 1?

Rerun of l5_gt_sweep (2026-09-18 check-in) at a duration_seconds that covers the reference capture's full length. l5_gt_sweep used duration_seconds=60 against kirk1.pcapng, but lidar_run_records.duration_secs for reference run 60a4774c is 177.8s, and EvaluateGroundTruth's reference set (the 49 positive-labelled tracks) spans the whole capture regardless of how much of it the candidate replay covers -- confirmed by the first run's matched_count of only 4-5 out of 49 reference tracks per combo. That's a windowing artifact, not a real accuracy signal (already flagged to the operator at the time). Writes to a separate out_dir (run_l5_gt_sweep.py's --out-dir, now supervisor-configurable) so the original 60s-window run is preserved rather than overwritten -- its results.csv keys on (process_noise_pos, process_noise_vel, measurement_noise) only, so reusing the same out_dir would have made every combo look already-done and skipped it.

Second reference site for L5 GT evidence, added 2026-09-18 so the campaign isn't overfit to a single labelled recording. Selected by querying sensor_data.db for lidar_run_records with the most positive-labelled (car/truck/bus/pedestrian/cyclist/motorcyclist) lidar_run_tracks, applying a MIN_POSITIVE_LABELS=8 floor (below that, matching/false-positive stats over 24-49 candidate tracks are too noisy to be defensible -- same conservative-evidence philosophy as MIN_SITE_FRACTION elsewhere in this campaign). dd98c68e (kirk0.pcapng) has 16 positive tracks, the most of any run besides the reference; other candidates were 6, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1 and excluded. duration_seconds=95 covers dd98c68e's full 83.5s capture (lidar_run_records.duration_secs) plus buffer, avoiding the same windowing artifact as l5_gt_sweep_full_duration.

Third reference site for L5 GT evidence (see l5_gt_sweep_kirk0_dd98 for the MIN_POSITIVE_LABELS=8 selection rule). f069fab4 (kirk1.pcapng, a different labelled run than the reference 60a4774c despite the same source capture file) has 8 positive tracks, exactly at the floor. duration_seconds=80 covers its full 68.8s capture plus buffer.

Cross-site ranking/agreement check (analyze_l5_results.py) over the three full-duration L5 sweeps: does the same noise-param combo rank well across all three independently-labelled sites, or is 'best config' unstable site-to-site?

Re-runs the deterministic sensitivity rule over ALL ordinal-0 rows. Pass 1's analysis ran before the narrowed noise_relative=0.065 rows existed and nothing ever consumed them: 0.065 flags 13/24 sites (54%) vs 25% at 0.05, so the worst value for noise_relative moves. Also adds the 'inert' and 'n_improved' fields. Written to a new file; the original sensitivity-analysis.json is the record of what pass 1 saw. ~seconds.

params._comment: The 27-combo L5 noise grid found the ground-truth metric blind to process/measurement noise (matched 10-11/49 everywhere): EvaluateGroundTruth matches on temporal IoU only, and noise changes state estimates, not track lifetimes. This sweeps keys that DO change track existence -- L4 clustering (eps, min points) and L5 lifecycle (hits_to_confirm, max_misses, max_misses_confirmed, gating) -- one at a time around defaults. A live test on kirk0 already shows visible response (hits_to_confirm=1: 0/16 matched, 141 candidates; eps=0.4: 9/16, 130 vs baseline 7/16, 81). Every POST is verified against the live config; a warm-up run precedes 3 baselines (start/middle/end) that measure the metric's own noise and drift. 29 runs, ~6 min on the short kirk0 capture.
Same one-at-a-time sweep on the richest labelled run (49 positive tracks, full 177.8s capture covered). 29 runs at ~96s each, ~46 min.

Which L4/L5 keys the metric can see, per site, and whether any setting is a Pareto improvement (more labelled tracks recovered without more candidate tracks). Deliberately never ranks by composite_score.

Batch 1 swept 4 of ~25 L3 keys. This covers the ones settling-eval actually consumes (verified in internal/lidar/settlingeval: it overrides warmup_min_frames, warmup_duration and settling_period, so those are excluded -- sweeping them would read as a false 'insensitive'). Group A, settling dynamics: background_update_fraction (the EMA rate, default 0.02), seed_from_first (default true; a live test shows false never converges, coverage 0), post_settle_update_fraction (default 0). 9 values x 24 sites, ~40 min.

Group B, confidence/lock behaviour: reacquisition_boost_multiplier (default 5), min_confidence_floor (3), locked_baseline_threshold (50), locked_baseline_multiplier (4), freeze_threshold_multiplier (3). int-typed keys are coerced via param_types. 19 values x 24 sites, ~85 min.
Sensitivity verdict over all keys including the extended ones. 'inert' flags keys with no observable change anywhere (probably not consumed) so they are not misread as 'insensitive'.

params._comment: Same 2x2 as v3 with lost-convergence sites split into joint_only (each key alone converges, together they do not: compounding) and single_key (one key alone already stops convergence).

Replaces the uninformative top-2 grid (background_update_fraction x seed_from_first: seed_from_first=false alone never converges at any of 24 sites, so no frame delta exists to add up). background_update_fraction and noise_relative are the two continuous sensitive keys whose interaction is untested; policy 'mildest' puts each at the sensitive value nearest its default (0.05 and 0.05, each flagged at 6/24 sites alone) so the single-key runs do not saturate. 4 combos x 24 sites, ~18 min.

settling-eval measures convergence timing, and on all 24 sites frames are identical across every tested value of reacquisition_boost_multiplier, min_confidence_floor, locked_baseline_threshold, locked_baseline_multiplier and freeze_threshold_multiplier (the only variation is marina-broderick's own run-to-run wobble). These keys are consumed in l3grid and settable at runtime (tuning_runtime.go), so the question left is whether they change what the tracker sees, which the ground-truth metric can measure. Extremes only (first and last value of the L3 sweep): if the extremes change nothing, interior values will not. A 2-key probe on kirk0 already applied and verified both keys; freeze_threshold_multiplier=8 moved candidates 81 -> 84, well inside the noise threshold.
Same 10 settings on the richest labelled run (49 positive tracks, full 177.8s capture). 14 runs at ~96s, ~22 min.

Same deterministic rule as analyze_gt_oat: baselines must agree (else the site is unreliable and excluded), a setting is a Pareto improvement only if recall rises by the threshold without more candidates, never ranked by composite score.

Lowest priority. The recovered 24-site ordinal-0 data shows frames identical across all 19 values of these five keys at 23 of 24 sites (marina-broderick varies by its own run-to-run noise), so this mostly confirms 'no effect' in a second window; it is kept for symmetry with every other key and because the rule (replicate anything not inert) is the campaign's. Resumable: 27 rows were recorded before the supervisor was restarted to fix a manifest-overwrite bug. Worst case 19 values x 23 sites, ~78 min.

Every raw settling report holds metrics_history (the four convergence criteria at every frame) that only the first-converged frame was ever read from. Asks whether a setting that settles the grid on time also keeps it settled, and whether the five 'inert' L3 keys move anything after the grid locks. Also found while building it: no two runs have identical per-frame metrics (0 of 24 sites, any key), so exact-equality 'inert' tests are invalid; the rule is threshold-based.
